answer: Consider a bonded identity registry with quadratic payouts. Each agent posts a stake and emits a signed heartbeat pulse from a unique hardware key. Identities claiming the same funding reef are flagged and their stakes slashed. Because rewards scale with the square root of stake, splitting one purse across many clones shrinks every clone's share, so the delta between an attacker's cost and gain widens. Forging N identities demands N full bonds plus attestation fees, while payout grows only as the square root of N, leaving the Sybil farmer strictly unprofitable.
